pages.page_summary: This page contains a series of physics problems (5.17 through 5.23) related to work, energy, and power. It includes a diagram (Fig. 5.15) illustrating a pendulum collision scenario.
knowledge_points: Problem 5.17: A pendulum bob A (mass m) released from 30° to the vertical hits another bob B (mass m) at rest on a table. The collision is elastic. The question asks for the height bob A rises after the collision.

Problem 5.18: A pendulum bob is released from a horizontal position with a length of 1.5 m. It dissipates 5% of its initial energy against air resistance. The question asks for the speed at the lowermost point.

Problem 5.19: A trolley of mass 300 kg carrying a sandbag of 25 kg moves at 27 km/h on a frictionless track. Sand leaks out at 0.05 kg/s. The question asks for the speed of the trolley after the sandbag is empty.

Problem 5.20: A body of mass 0.5 kg travels in a straight line with velocity v = ax^(3/2) where a = 5 m^(-1/2) s^(-1). The question asks for the work done by the net force during displacement from x = 0 to x = 2 m.

Problem 5.21: Windmill blades sweep out a circle of area A. Wind flows at velocity v perpendicular to the circle. Questions ask for mass of air passing through in time t, kinetic energy of the air, and electrical power produced given specific values (A=30 m², v=36 km/h, density=1.2 kg/m³, 25% efficiency).

Problem 5.22: A person lifts a 10 kg mass 1000 times to a height of 0.5 m. Questions ask for work done against gravity and the amount of fat used up given fat energy content (3.8 x 10^7 J/kg) and 20% efficiency.

Problem 5.23: A family uses 8 kW of power. Direct solar energy is incident at 200 W/m². 20% is converted to electrical energy. Questions ask for the area needed to supply 8 kW and a comparison to a typical house roof.

visuals.description: A diagram showing a pendulum bob A suspended from a pivot, released from an angle of 30 degrees to the vertical. It swings down to hit another bob B of the same mass (m) resting on a horizontal surface. The diagram shows the initial position of A and the position of B.
visuals.educational_role: Illustrates the setup for the physics problem 5.17 regarding elastic collision between two pendulum bobs.
